cards.title: Pick your tiers
cards.text: Every tier I made, lowest to highest, the six in use among them. Tick the ones you like.
cards.why: You asked for a board to pick from, up and down, into the abstract. Once you pick, I set where each one starts. Pin anything that looks wrong.
cards.details:
There are 25 new ones and the six in use. Each one is a line in the same table as the tiers in use, drawn with the same shared parts (metal, grain, cut gems, sky, drifting colour, glowing core, the black hole) and its own colours and extras, so a tier you keep is ready, and one you drop costs nothing.

Each film is six seconds and loops, shown bigger than on the phone, at a count I'd guess for it. Those counts and the 'below bronze' or 'past aurora' notes are suggestions only: nothing new has a starting count yet.

Shields: tiers below bronze have none, bronze to gold one, the rest two. Untick the six in use to drop or replace one.

My picks lean on the ones you named (wood, tin, platinum, eternal, legendary, omnipotent) plus the ones I think read clearest small.

cards.title: Bronze, losing it, shields
cards.text: Bronze lost its thin line. A miss now cracks the chip while a shield is left, and shatters it when none is.
cards.why: Your notes from 0.5: the thin line, a shatter instead of the fade, the width never jumping, and your shields. Pin anything that looks wrong.
cards.details:
To update: close Primer fully and open it again; Profile shows 0.5.3 at the bottom. Shields and the shatter are live in Review.

Shields only protect the count. A missed fact still comes back a few questions later and is due sooner in your memory, exactly as before.

The films come from the tests, with a made-up topic, shown bigger than on the phone, without the question below. The crack and shatter films have their sound in them; the phone plays films silent, so the sounds are also on the shields part to tap.

If your phone is set to reduce motion, cracks still show and the chip still empties, but nothing knocks or flies.

parts.title: Bronze
parts.text: The thin bright line along its band is gone. Silver and gold still have theirs.

parts.title: Losing it: a shatter
parts.text: With no shield left, cracks run right through the chip, it swells a touch and bursts: the pieces fly out, turn, fall and fade, and plain ×0 comes up under them. A crunch and a few glassy notes if Effects is on. The chip doesn't change width: it keeps the widest it has been in the run, and grows smoothly when a count needs another digit.

parts.title: Shields and cracks
parts.text: Bronze to gold take one miss, crystal and up two. A miss with a shield left knocks the chip and opens a crack across it, with a small crack sound; the count and pips stay. One crack shows per shield used. Right answers don't mend cracks; reaching the next tier does. Here: gold's one crack, crystal's second, a tier-up mending one, and the whole run of it.

cards.title: When shields come back
cards.text: Do shields refill when you reach a new tier, and stay used until then?
cards.why: Right answers mending cracks would make a shield nearly free: miss, get one right, miss again. Refilling only at a new tier keeps a crack meaning something while still rewarding a long run.
cards.pick: Yes: reaching a new tier refills them and mends the cracks; right answers don't.
cards.details:
Other ways it could go: a crack mends after five right in a row (one full row of pips), or shields only come back when a new run starts.

The film on the shields part shows the way it works now: gold cracked at ×24, one right answer reaches crystal, and the cracked chip fades as the clean one swells.
